question: Název karetní hry mariáš pochází z francouzštiny. Co to francouzské slovo znamená?
source_excerpt: The name comes from the French card game Mariage... 'mariage' (marriage or wedding)

extra.why_interesting: Czechs say 'mariáš' all their lives without thinking of it as a foreign word. The French sound of the word gives a foothold to work it out, and the payoff is that the king and svršek in a hláška form a married couple.
extra.verification_notes: Czech Wikipedia confirms mariáš derives from French 'mariage' (marriage/wedding), matching 'Sňatek'.

explanation: Francouzské slovo „mariage“ znamená sňatek a hra je pojmenovaná po hlášce: král a svršek stejné barvy tvoří „manželský pár“, za který se připisují body.

question: V běžné hře mariáše je hned pod esem jediná karta s číslem, která přebije i krále. Která to je?
source_excerpt: In trump contracts, every suit ranks from high to low: ace, ten, king, over, under, nine, eight, seven.

extra.why_interesting: Non-players assume picture cards beat number cards, so a king should beat a ten. In mariáš, a 'mere' number card outranks the king. The clue 'right below the ace' makes it reachable, and the twist about betl and durch rewards anyone who has played.
extra.verification_notes: In the standard (trump) game of mariáš the ranking is ace, ten, king, over, under, 9, 8, 7, so the ten is the only numbered card between the ace and the king; the ten ranks lower only in Betl/Durch, which are not the ordinary game (https://www.pagat.com/marriage/marias.html).

explanation: Desítka je v mariáši druhá nejsilnější karta a spolu s esem vynáší po deseti bodech. Jen v betlu a durchu klesne do přirozeného pořadí, pod spodka.
